newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: PBOC will continue same monetary policy -Guo You.
newsitem.headline: PBOC will continue same monetary policy -Guo You.

text.p: The People's Bank of China (PBOC) will continue to pursue moderately tight monetary policy in 1997, even though macro monetary regulation has been achieved in the last several years, a Chinese official said.

Guo You, Deputy Director of the Foreign Financial Institutions Department of the People's Bank of China told a conference in Singapore, "Once the central bank relaxes control of money there will emerge quickly a new cycle of economic expansion and inflation."
"The moderately tight monetary policy is a medium-term policy, it provides a favourable macroecnomic environment for sustained, rapid and healthy economic growth...," he added.

The reform of indirect regulation will be speeded up with measures which include changes of the operating target of monetary policy, the reform of the asset and liability account of the central bank and the improvement of the system of deposit.
The size and category of transactions of the national interbank market will be gradually increased and open market operation of the central bank will be further promoted, Guo said.
Guo added the market in negotiable instruments will be pushed forward and market forces, supply and demand, will play a greater role in the interest rate structure.
There will be further coordination of domestic and external monetary policy, via a stable exchange rate, and credit policy will be further brought into play to enhance stable economic growth.
On top of this Guo said the central bank is continuing to promote order in the financial sector, promote financial supervision and work towards a stable performance of the financial industry.

"The next step of China's reform and development would be to continue the implementation of moderately tight monetary policy, make a real effort to strengthen financial supervision and regulation, improve the means of financial adjustment, overhaul financial structure and make full use of a variety of monetary policy instruments to control the monetary aggregates," he said.
